narrative.overview: This is a category-standard portfolio (a chosen "canon" build) executed at a craft bar set against rauno.me, joshwcomeau.com, and linear.app, rather than a themed metaphor world. The system reads as a precise, quiet instrument for one job: let a recruiter confirm in seconds that this person can ship at both big-tech rigor and startup speed. Near-black graphite replaces the site's two prior looks; this pass deliberately breaks from both, and from the warm-cream-plus-serif pattern AI-generated portfolios default to. Restraint is the whole argument: one neutral scale, one accent color, two self-hosted typefaces, no gradients, no glow, no glassmorphism.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black graphite ground with a single confident, non-neon emerald accent used flat
Two self-hosted typefaces (Cabinet Grotesk display, Satoshi body) — no system-font-as-display-voice
One authored motion moment (hero load-in) plus one signature interaction (project-tile hover reveal)
Real, verified content only; no invented metrics, testimonials, or claims

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Emerald appears only on interactive or single-emphasis moments. It never fills a background region or appears twice in the same static viewport.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only on timeline years and technology-name tags — never nav labels, headings, or link text.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no blur-based glow, no gradient standing in for a shadow. Depth is tonal-step layering only.

dos: Do keep emerald to interactive/single-emphasis moments only
Do give every section a real, standalone heading — no eyebrow/kicker labels
Do reserve JetBrains Mono for genuine data
Do keep motion to one load-in moment plus the project-tile hover reveal
Do verify any new text color against both bg and surface at ≥4.5:1
donts: Don't add a gradient, glow, or blur-based halo anywhere
Don't hide a project's name or description behind hover-only content
Don't reintroduce a kicker/eyebrow label above a heading
Don't add a second accent color
Don't fabricate or embellish a resume fact
